messages:
Maya (SRE): OpsBot fired a huge wave of alerts for kv-cacher at 03:14 UTC. Lots of noisy PD pages. I’m in the thread.
OpsBot: Incident opened: INC-2026-5298 — high 5xx rate on service=kv-cacher. initial_alert_count=312. routed_to=#eng-oncall.
Ben (oncall): seeing it. Customers reporting elevated error rates for embeddings calls. PD is noisy — getting multiple pages. 
Carlos (support): several tickets just came in from CustomerA about failed uploads. Tagging product for impact. @Emma FYI.
Priya (eng-sre): quick assessment: root cause looks like transient backend overload after a borked config push — many pods restarted and the KV warm cache dropped, causing spike in origin 5xxs. Not a platform-wide regression. 
Maya (SRE): short-term plan: 1) temporary PD suppression/dedupe 2) raise noisy alert thresholds for kv-cacher 3) add dashboard slices for customer impact 4) schedule follow-up for durable fixes. Ideas? :thinking_face:
Ben (oncall): please do the suppression now — my phone is melting. Can we squelch PD for kv-cacher for 30m and route aggregated alert to oncall channel only?
OpsBot: /squelch incident INC-2026-5298 --service kv-cacher --duration 30m — created suppression SQUELCH-477. Notifies channel only, no PD pages.
Nikhil (alerts): I applied a quick dedupe rule on the alert pipeline to collapse events with identical trace_id and pod labels. That should cut duplicates by ~70%. Also added a rate limit: max 6 alerts/min per service.
Priya (eng-sre): I also pushed a temporary change to the Prom rule for High5xxRate to avoid thrashing from short spikes. Old rule:
```
- alert: High5xxRate
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"kv-cacher\",code=~\"5..\"}[2m])) by (pod) > 20
  for: 1m
```
New (temporary):
```
- alert: High5xxRateKvCacher_temp
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"kv-cacher\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (service) > 75
  for: 3m
```
This raises the bar and increases the window; we can revert after spike settles.
Ben (oncall): good. That stopped the paging within 90s. thanks. Can we also downgrade PD severity for this class to 'low' while squelch is active?
Maya (SRE): done — updated PD routing: kv-cacher -> escalation: low. If the dedupe and squelch miss anything we still get channel notification.
Carlos (support): CustomerA impact: moderate for ~12 minutes, then intermittent until now. I filed a support ticket and linked logs to the incident: https://redwood-support/INC-2026-5298/logs.
Jin (infra): note: the underlying restarts were caused by a bad liveness tweak rolled at 03:00. Rolling back that flag reduces pod churn. I started the rollback; pods are stabilizing.
Priya (eng-sre): putting notes for post-incident follow-ups: - add per-service adaptive thresholding based on baseline traffic - build a dashboard that correlates pod restarts, KV hit rate, and 5xxs - implement alert grouping by root_cause_tag and customer_tier - propose PD routing tweak to send aggregated alerts to a single escalation instead of page floods.
Nikhil (alerts): for the dashboard, here's a quick grafana query I used to validate impact:
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"kv-cacher\",code=~\"5..\"}[1m])) by (customer_id)
```
I'll add a dashboard panel for top-10 affected customers and an annotation for when squelch started.
Maya (SRE): decision log: short-term changes applied: squelch(SQUELCH-477), temp rule High5xxRateKvCacher_temp, dedupe pipeline rule, PD severity lowered. Action owner list below.
- Follow-up (Priya): design adaptive thresholds + grouping strategy — due EOD tomorrow.
- Alerts (Nikhil): implement grouping by trace_id + add PD rate-limit on integration — due in 3 days.
- Infra (Jin): confirm rollback fully rolled out and add guardrails to prevent similar liveness changes — due today.
- Support (Carlos): send incident impact summary to CustomerA and include mitigation timeline — due in 2 hours.
Ben (oncall): thanks team. My phone cooled off :grin:. Tagging for visibility: @here this is contained and we’ve applied temp mitigations.
OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-5298 status changed to mitigated (squelch active, root cause identified). Follow-up epic: INC-2026-5298-FU created: https://tracker/incidents/INC-2026-5298-FU
Priya (eng-sre): one technical note — dedupe by trace_id is great but we should also group by deployment_revision; many duplicates were from rapid restarts creating new pod labels. Grouping by stable identifiers will reduce noise more reliably.
Nikhil (alerts): agreed. I'll prototype grouping keys: {customer_id, root_cause_tag, deployment_revision}. Also adding a small backoff window so we don't reopen the same group within 10m.
Maya (SRE): ok. Closing immediate loop here. We'll lift squelch after 30m unless Jin calls it stable earlier. After that, schedule a 1-hour postmortem sync to finalize alerting changes and dashboard work.
Ben (oncall): ping me when the follow-up epic lands. I'll attend the postmortem.
Carlos (support): sending customer note now.
Jin (infra): rollback complete; pods stable. Marking my action done.
Maya (SRE): great work everyone. Lessons: temporary squelch + sensible thresholds + dedupe saved a lot of noise and reduced customer-facing impact. We'll make the longer-term changes permanent in the follow-up epic. :white_check_mark:
